- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement to prevent false rallies.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), reduce forecast momentum to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), adjust forecast downward with lagged smoothing.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and history shows volatility, avoid linear extrapolation; use weighted average of recent 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from initial forecast, re-calibrate early days to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0–0.2 spikes, expect short-term correction; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
